title: Comparable monotone maps give a prism homotopy on augmented strict poset chains
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P,Q$ finite partially ordered sets, possibly empty. Write $C(P;R)$ for the chain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] whose degree $n\geq0$ is free on strict chains $[x_0<\cdots<x_n]$ in $P$, whose degree $-1$ is $R$ on $[\varnothing]$, and whose lower degrees are zero. Its differential is alternating vertex deletion, including $d[x]=[\varnothing]$ in degree zero and $d[\varnothing]=0$. In formulas, a weakly increasing tuple with a repeated entry denotes zero. For every monotone map $u:P\to Q$, the rule $u_*[x_0<\cdots<x_n]=[u(x_0)\leq\cdots\leq u(x_n)]$ and $u_*[\varnothing]=[\varnothing]$ defines a chain map $C(P;R)\to C(Q;R)$. These chain maps preserve identities and composition. If $f,g:P\to Q$ are monotone with $f(x)\leq g(x)$ for every $x$, the $R$-linear maps
$$h_n[x_0<\cdots<x_n]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[f(x_0)\leq\cdots\leq f(x_i)\leq g(x_i)\leq\cdots\leq g(x_n)]\quad(n\geq0),\qquad h_{-1}=0$$
(and zero in lower degrees) satisfy $dh+hd=g_*-f_*$ in every integer degree.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-poset-weak-chain-normalization] to $P$ and $Q$. It gives augmented weak-chain complexes $W$, repeated-tuple subcomplexes $D$, and chain isomorphisms $\overline q_S:W(S)/D(S)\cong C(S;R)$. Thus the differential on the strict-chain modules in the statement is the quotient differential, including the vertex-to-empty augmentation.

proof.text: For a monotone $u:P\to Q$, [lem-sfb-poset-weak-chain-normalization] gives a chain map $W(u)$ preserving $D$. Its quotient map, conjugated by $\overline q_P$ and $\overline q_Q$, sends a strict generator to the entrywise image with repeated tuples killed and fixes the empty generator. This is exactly $u_*$. The equations $W(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $W(v\circ u)=W(v)W(u)$ pass to the quotients and then through these isomorphisms, proving both functoriality assertions.

proof.text:
For the given comparable $f,g$, [lem-sfb-poset-weak-prism-identity] supplies $H_n$ preserving $D$ and satisfying $d^Q_{n+1}H_n+H_{n-1}d^P_n=W(g)_n-W(f)_n$. It induces maps on $W/D$. By [lem-sfb-poset-weak-chain-normalization], the quotient identifications send each weak pivot tuple to its strict bracket, killing repetitions, so these induced maps are exactly the displayed $h_n$. Explicitly, $q_{Q,n+1}H_n=h_nq_{P,n}$ and $q_{Q,n}W(u)_n=u_{*,n}q_{P,n}$ on every basis tuple: repeated input tuples remain repeated, and strict tuples have precisely the stated image. Apply $q_{Q,n}$ to the weak identity. The chain-map equations for $q$ give
$$(d^C_{Q,n+1}h_n+h_{n-1}d^C_{P,n})q_{P,n}=(g_{*,n}-f_{*,n})q_{P,n}.$$
Cancel the surjective $q_{P,n}$ to obtain the assertion. In degree $-1$, both homotopy terms vanish and both induced maps fix the empty generator, so their difference is zero; below $-1$ the source vanishes. These checks include empty posets.

lean.statement: theorem prism_identity (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {P Q : Type v} [PartialOrder P] [PartialOrder Q] [Finite P] [Finite Q] (f g : P →o Q) (hfg : ∀ x : P, f x ≤ g x) (n : ℤ) : prismComponent R f g n (n + 1) ≫ (complex R Q).d (n + 1) n + (complex R P).d n (n - 1) ≫ prismComponent R f g (n - 1) n = (map R g).f n - (map R f).f n
